subject: paediatrics
title: Pediatric Platelet and Marrow Failure Disorders: VWD and Aplastic Anaemias

steps.tx: Deficiency or qualitative dysfunction of von Willebrand factor impairs platelet adhesion and circulating Factor VIII stability. As the most common inherited bleeding disorder, **pediatric von Willebrand disease** (VWD) is typically inherited in an autosomal dominant fashion. Because von Willebrand factor mediates platelet tethering to subendothelial collagen and protects Factor VIII from rapid degradation, affected children present with mucocutaneous bleeding, epistaxis, and menorrhagia.
steps.say: Von Willebrand disease is the commonest inherited bleeding disorder, causing mucocutaneous bleeding and epistaxis. It impairs platelet adhesion and Factor VIII stability.

vis.alt: Diagram demonstrating the dual role of von Willebrand factor in platelet adhesion and stabilizing circulating Factor VIII.
vis.caption: Dual haemostatic functions of von Willebrand factor in subendothelial platelet tethering and Factor VIII carrier binding. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Establishing the specific laboratory subtype of von Willebrand disease dictates tailored pharmacotherapeutic interventions. Type 1 represents quantitative partial reduction of structurally normal VWF (seventy-five percent of cases), Type 2 represents qualitative structural or functional defects, and **Type 3 von Willebrand disease** is an autosomal recessive, severe total absence of VWF with profound Factor VIII deficiency, mimicking severe hemophilia with spontaneous hemarthroses.
steps.say: Type one VWD is a mild quantitative reduction in VWF, while Type three is an autosomal recessive complete absence mimicking severe hemophilia with joint bleeds.

rows: Excellent for mucosal dental & oral bleeds

steps.tx: Acquired T-cell mediated autoimmune destruction of hematopoietic stem cells drives bone marrow hypocellularity. In children with **acquired aplastic anaemia**, autoreactive cytotoxic T lymphocytes secrete interferon-gamma and tumor necrosis factor, inducing stem cell apoptosis. Patients present with profound pancytopenia, marked pallor, petechiae, and mucosal bleeding, while physical examination demonstrates an absence of hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy.
steps.say: Acquired aplastic anemia involves autoimmune T-cell destruction of bone marrow stem cells, causing pancytopenia without hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy.

vis.alt: Bone marrow trephine biopsy showing severe hypocellularity with replacement of hematopoietic elements by adipose tissue.
vis.caption: Marked bone marrow hypocellularity with widespread adipocyte replacement in severe aplastic anaemia. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Standardized criteria established by Camitta categorize the severity of bone marrow hypocellularity and peripheral cytopenias. Diagnosis of **severe aplastic anaemia criteria** requires bone marrow cellularity below twenty-five percent on trephine core biopsy, accompanied by at least two of the following peripheral blood thresholds: absolute neutrophil count below five hundred per microlitre, platelet count below twenty thousand per microlitre, or reticulocyte count below twenty thousand.
steps.say: Severe aplastic anemia requires bone marrow cellularity below twenty-five percent plus an absolute neutrophil count under five hundred or platelets under twenty thousand.

rows: Induces remission in 70% lacking sibling donor
Eltrombopag (TPO agonist) added as triple therapy

steps.tx: Defective DNA cross-link repair mechanisms characterize the most prevalent inherited constitutional bone marrow failure syndrome. Inherited primarily as an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the FANC gene family, **Fanconi anaemia in children** presents with progressive bone marrow failure emerging between five and ten years of age, physical malformations, and extreme susceptibility to myeloid leukemia and solid tumors.
steps.say: Fanconi anemia is an inherited DNA repair defect causing progressive bone marrow failure between five and ten years, associated with physical anomalies and cancer risk.

left.title: Characteristic Physical Phenotype
points: Skeletal: hypoplastic or absent thumbs, absent radius
Cutaneous: generalized hyperpigmentation and café-au-lait spots
Growth: severe short stature and microcephaly
Renal: horseshoe kidneys, ectopic or absent kidneys

right.title: Definitive Diagnostic Test
points: Or mitomycin C (MMC) challenge on peripheral lymphocytes
Demonstrates dramatic increase in chromosomal radial figures
Confirms diagnosis prior to bone marrow transplantation

steps.tx: A distinct congenital pure erythroid marrow aplasia presents in early infancy with profound macrocytic anemia. Characterized by heterozygous mutations in ribosomal protein genes (RPS19 in twenty-five percent), **Diamond-Blackfan anaemia** manifests in infants under one year with severe normochromic macrocytic anemia, reticulocytopenia, and normal white blood cell and platelet counts. Bone marrow examination demonstrates a selective, profound absence of erythroid precursor cells.
steps.say: Diamond-Blackfan anemia is a congenital pure red cell aplasia caused by ribosomal protein mutations. Infants present under one year with severe macrocytic anemia and normal platelets.

steps.tx: Differentiating congenital ribosomopathies from self-limiting acquired red cell arrest prevents unnecessary chronic therapies. Typically occurring in previously healthy toddlers aged one to four years following a mild viral illness, **transient erythroblastopenia of childhood** (TEC) produces transient suppression of erythropoiesis. Unlike Diamond-Blackfan anemia, physical examination is completely normal, erythrocyte adenosine deaminase (eADA) activity is normal, and spontaneous recovery occurs within two months.
steps.say: Transient erythroblastopenia of childhood occurs in healthy toddlers after a viral illness. Unlike Diamond-Blackfan anemia, red cell adenosine deaminase is normal and recovery is spontaneous.

left.title: Transient Erythroblastopenia (TEC)
points: Onset in toddlers (1 to 4 years of age)

right.title: Diamond-Blackfan Treatment
points: Oral prednisolone (2 mg/kg/day) induces remission in 80%
Wean to lowest alternate-day steroid dose
Chronic packed RBC transfusions with iron chelation
Allogeneic HSCT is definitive curative treatment

steps.tx: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation represents the definitive curative intervention for constitutional and severe acquired marrow failure. Utilizing a matched sibling donor, **hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in aplastic anaemia** provides cure rates exceeding eighty to ninety percent. Conditioning regimens are carefully tailored, using reduced-intensity regimens in Fanconi anemia due to hypersensitivity to DNA-damaging alkylating agents.
steps.say: Allogeneic stem cell transplantation from a matched sibling donor offers a ninety percent cure rate for severe aplastic anemia. Fanconi anemia requires reduced-intensity conditioning.

rows: 70 to 80 percent with modern graft engineering
Avoid full-dose irradiation and toxic alkylators
